DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.claim: Aflaha can mean becoming happy or blessed.
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r7.anchor: افلح سعد قوله تعالى في سورة المؤمنين قد افلح المؤمنون يعني سعدوا وقال تعالى في سورة سبح قد افلح من تزكى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.claim: The soul mirrors the larger world: God inspires good and evil, inclines it to good and against evil, and requires it to preserve balance; unchecked evil leads to arrogance and disorder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.anchor: inclined it towards good and made it hate evil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.claim: The soul itself witnesses its Maker’s purpose: awareness of good and evil entails adopting good and avoiding evil; success is purification and failure is sin, so denying accountability contradicts this witness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.anchor: the awareness of good and evil is found in it. Obviously, the reason for giving him this awareness is that man should adopt good and shield himself from evil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r2.claim: Because people can distinguish good from evil, they must choose good and shun evil; this brings success, while vice leads to misery.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r2.anchor: When a person has been given the awareness of good and evil, then it is his obligation to adopt good and shun evil.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.claim: Using every divine favour rightly serves one’s own interest and expresses gratitude; failing to do so is self-destruction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.anchor: every favour God has bestowed on him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.claim: As a person who closes his eyes risks falling and bears responsibility, a person must stay alert to the moral path he follows.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.anchor: there is a strong probability that he might fall in a pit and he himself would be responsible for this mishap and no other person.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r6.claim: Some take 91:9–10 as the oath’s complement; Islahi gives weight to al-Zamakhsharī’s rejection of that view.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r6.anchor: there is weight in his rejection.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r2.claim: The purification and corruption statement explains one aspect of the final oath rather than serving as its complement; Islahi endorses al-Zamakhsharī’s view that the complement is suppressed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r2.anchor: a suppression of the muqsam ‘alayh has occurred here.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.claim: Suppressing the complement lets everything evident from the oaths count as its content; one prominent implication is that God destroys rebellious nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.anchor: The benefit of this suppression is that everything

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.claim: Al-Layl develops the preceding sūrah’s claim that the soul succeeds through purification by identifying what corrupts it and how it can be protected and purified.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.anchor: the things which contaminate it are explained

QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r5.claim: The successful person purifies the soul, or is purified by God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r5.anchor: ويقال : من زكاه الله عز وجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r1.speaker: الرسول
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r1.claim: A prophetic supplication asks God to purify the soul, since He is the best to purify it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r1.anchor: والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «وزكها أنت خير من زكاها» .

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.claim: The mention of taqwā is followed by success for the one who purifies himself, and failure is followed by mention of the people of Paradise as a counterpoint.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r3.anchor: وحين قال: وتقواها أعقبه بقوله: قد أفلح من زكاها.

FARRA:v3p266/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p266/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p266/r7.claim: One explanation makes God the subject: the soul He purifies succeeds, and the soul He hides away fails.
FARRA:v3p266/r7.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: قد أفلح من زكاها (9) يقول: قد أفلحت نفس زكاها الله، وقد خابت نفس دساها،

FARRA:v3p266/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p266/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p266/r8.claim: Another explanation makes the person the subject: one succeeds by purifying the soul through obedience and charity and fails by neglecting both.
FARRA:v3p266/r8.anchor: ويقال: قد أفلح من زكى نفسه بالطاعة والصدقة، وقد خاب من دسى نفسه،

NAHHAS:v5p235/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p235/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p235/r10.claim: He says the one who succeeds is the one whose soul God purifies.
NAHHAS:v5p235/r10.anchor: روى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه

NAHHAS:v5p235/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p235/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p235/r12.claim: If God is the subject of purifying, the relative pronoun cannot straightforwardly resume an element of its own clause; possible workarounds treat man as soul or as a group.
NAHHAS:v5p235/r12.anchor: وذلك أنه إذا كان الضمير يعود على الله جل وعز لم يعد على من من صلته شيء إلا على حيلة بعيدة

NAHHAS:v5p235/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p235/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p235/r13.claim: God's purification means enabling obedience; zakā for wealth can mean either growth by paying alms or cleansing wealth by giving the poor their share.
NAHHAS:v5p235/r13.anchor: ومعنى زكاها الله طهرها بالتوفيق لطاعته وزكى فلان ماله في اشتقاقه قولان أحدهما أنه من زكا الزرع إذا زاد ونما

NAHHAS:v5p235/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p235/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p235/r14.claim: The alternative derivation makes zakā mean purifying and freeing wealth through the poor's share; zakiyya and zakī likewise mean pure.
NAHHAS:v5p235/r14.anchor: والقول الآخر بين حسن يكون زكى ماله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses purifying the soul as reforming it.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r7.anchor: قد افلح من زكاها قال : اصلحها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r16.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r16.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r16.claim: The Prophet says the soul succeeds when God purifies it.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r16.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول في قوله الله : قد افلح من زكاها قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' افلحت نفس زكاها الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r18.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r18.claim: Ibn Abbas says the successful soul is one God purifies.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r18.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : قد افلح من زكاها بقول : قد افلح من زكى الله نفسه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3438/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3438/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3438/r1.claim: The Prophet says a soul succeeds when God purifies it and fails when deprived of all good.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3438/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : قد افلح من زكاها الاية : ' افلحت نفس زكاها الله وخابت نفس خيبها الله من كل خير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.claim: The oath is prepared by noting that purifying the soul leads to success, while neglecting its reform leads to immorality and loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.anchor: ومهد لذلك بالتنبيه على أن تزكية النفس سبب الفلاح ، وأن التقصير في إصلاحها سبب الفجور والخسران .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.claim: Inspiring vice and piety means making their difference clear and enabling choice; the following verses show the human being performs purification or defilement, which respectively elevate through piety or diminish through sin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r8.anchor: ومعنى إلهام الفجور والتقوى : إفهامهما وإعقالهما ، وأن أحدهما حسن والآخر قبيح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r9.claim: Asked about the words, Ibn Abbas points to ‘successful is the one who purifies himself’ and ‘he has failed who bears wrongdoing.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r9.anchor: أتقرأ : { قد أفلح من تزكى } ، ( الأعلى : 14 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r10.claim: The claim that God is the agent of purifying and defiling is, in the author's view, a distortion by Qadariyya who falsely attribute reprehensible destiny to God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r10.anchor: وأما قول من زعم أن الضمير في زكى ودسى لله تعالى ، وأن تأنيث الراجع إلى من

RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.claim: The sura urges obedience and warns against disobedience; oaths by beneficial created things prompt reflection and gratitude because divine oaths weigh heavily on the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.anchor: المقصود من هذه السورة الترغيب في الطاعات والتحذير من المعاصي

RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r4.speaker: القراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r4.claim: Readers vary between imala and full pronunciation in this sura's verse endings, sometimes applying imala throughout and sometimes only selectively.
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r4.anchor: القراء مختلفون في فواصل هذه السورة وما أشبهها

RAZI-FULL:v31p172/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p172/r1.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p172/r1.claim: Seven things are sworn by through 'successful indeed' as the oath's answer; al-Zajjaj says the lām of laqad is omitted because the long passage substitutes for it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p172/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج : المعنى لقد أفلح ، لكن اللام حذفت لأن الكلام طال

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.claim: An eight-verse oath series leads into the antithetical statement in verses 9–10; the pre-Islamic genre is repurposed in verses 5–7 to express biblical creation ideas.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.anchor: mit anschließender, antithetischer Schwuraussage (V. 9.10). Die Schwurserie

TABRISI:91:1-15/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:1-15/r17.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:91:1-15/r17.claim: Success is purifying and reforming the soul through obedience and righteous deeds; Qatada agrees.
TABRISI:91:1-15/r17.anchor: قد أفلح من زكى نفسه عن الحسن وقتادة أي طهرها وأصلحها بطاعة الله

TABRISI:91:1-15/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:1-15/r19.speaker: سعيد بن أبي هلال
TABRISI:91:1-15/r19.claim: The Prophet reportedly paused when reciting this verse and prayed for his soul's piety and purification.
TABRISI:91:1-15/r19.anchor: وجاءت الرواية عن سعيد بن أبي هلال قال

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r9.claim: After the oaths, the surah's central message is responsibility: the one who purifies the soul succeeds, while the one who lets it follow evil loses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r9.anchor: 1-8. âyetlerde yer alan yemin ifadelerinden sonra 9-10. âyetlerde sûrenin asıl mesajı olan insanın sorumluluğuna dikkat çekilmiş

QASHANI:91:9-10/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:91:9-10/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:91:9-10/r1.claim: The successful reach perfection and the original fitra by purifying the soul.
QASHANI:91:9-10/r1.anchor: بالوصول إلى الكمال وبلوغ الفطرة الأولى

QASHANI:91:9-10/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:91:9-10/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:91:9-10/r3.claim: The oath’s omitted answer is that veiled deniers of the Prophet will perish through transgression as Thamud did, because they reject the inspiration, remain sinful, veil intellect, and let the dark self dominate.
QASHANI:91:9-10/r3.anchor: ليّهلكن المحجوبون المكذبون للنبي بطغيانهم كما أهلكت ثمود لتكذيبهم نبيهم بطغيانهم

SULAMI:v2p397#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r1.claim: The successful person is enabled to attend carefully to his moments.
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : لمن وفق لمراعات أوقاته

SULAMI:v2p397#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r2.claim: Success belongs to one granted insight into what is appointed for him.
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r2.anchor: قال سهل : افلح من رزق النظر أمر ميعاده

SULAMI:v2p397#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r3.claim: Success means examining where one's food comes from; failure is neglecting that.
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عثمان المغربي : افلح من نظر من أين مطعمه

SULAMI:v2p397#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r4.claim: Success protects the inner secret from worldly pollution; failure occupies that secret with the world.
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : افلح من طهر ستره عن التدنس بالدنيا

SULAMI:v2p397#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r5.claim: Success is knowing what God requires and addresses to one; failure is neglecting it.
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : افلح من علم ما يراد منه وما يخاطب به

SULAMI:v2p397#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r6.claim: Success is constant worship and service to God without taking another deity.
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أفلح من داوم على العبادة والعبودية لربه

SULAMI:v2p397#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r7.claim: The successful turn toward their Lord, and the unsuccessful turn away.
SULAMI:v2p397#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أفلح من أقبل على ربه ، وخاب من اعرض عنه

IBNASHUR:91:9/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:9/r1.claim: The sentence may answer the oath, promising the believers' success and the polytheists' failure, as the oath response does in al-Layl.
IBNASHUR:91:9/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الجملة جواب القسم ، وإن المعنى تحقيق فلاح المؤمنين وخَيبة المشركين

IBNASHUR:91:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:9/r2.claim: Alternatively, it may interrupt the oath before its answer, linking God's inspiration of vice and piety to the success of one who purifies the soul and follows piety.
IBNASHUR:91:9/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جملةً معترضة بين القَسم والجواب لمناسبة ذكر إلهام الفجور والتقوى

IBNASHUR:91:9/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:9/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:9/r3.claim: This prepares for the account of Thamūd: their punishment exemplifies the failure of those who pollute themselves with transgression.
IBNASHUR:91:9/r3.anchor: فإن ما أصاب ثمودا كان من خيبتهم

IBNASHUR:91:9/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:9/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:9/r4.claim: Success comes first to match piety; failure follows to prepare the transition to Thamūd's punishment for moral corruption.
IBNASHUR:91:9/r4.anchor: وقدم الفلاح على الخيبة لمناسبته للتقوى ، وأردف بخيبة من دسى نفسه لتهيئة الانتقال

IBNASHUR:91:9/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:9/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:9/r5.claim: The one who purifies is the human being, with the self and person treated as two things because of intention and acquired action.
IBNASHUR:91:9/r5.anchor: الإِنسان والنفس شيء واحد ، ونزلا منزلة شيئين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r4.claim: The success-and-failure statement may answer the oath, like the answer in Sūrat al-Layl, or interrupt it to explain that the soul succeeds by choosing its divinely indicated piety.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r4.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الجملة جواب القسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.claim: This contrast prepares the lesson of Thamūd: their punishment followed from corrupting their souls through arrogance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.anchor: وهذه الجملة توطئة لجملة : كذبت ثمود بطغواها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r6.claim: The human who purifies the soul and that soul are the same being, presented as two because of choice and action; tazkiyah means increasing goodness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r6.anchor: فالإنسان والنفس شيء واحد ، ونزلا منزلة شيئين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.claim: If success and failure answer the oath, Thamūd's denial is evidence for the failure of those who corrupt their souls.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.anchor: في موقع الدليل لمضمون جملة { وقد خاب من دساها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r2.claim: Success is attaining one's aim and failure is being deprived of it; lasting good is true success, while transient gain that turns into decline is failure, ultimately in the afterlife.

TUSTARI:91:9/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:91:9/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:91:9/r1.claim: The successful person is granted insight into the affairs of the afterlife.
TUSTARI:91:9/r1.anchor: قال: أفلح من رزق النظر في أمر معاده.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r8.claim: The oath's response is qad aflaha, with an implied la; the subject of zakāh may be God, purifying a group, or the person who purifies himself by acquiring goodness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r8.anchor: وجواب القسم في قوله قد أفلح، التقدير: لقد أفلح، والفاعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r9.claim: Zakkāh means purifying and nourishing the soul through good deeds; dassāhā means hiding and degrading it through sin and withholding required charity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r9.anchor: وزكاها معناه: طهرها ونماها بالخيرات، ودساها معناه: أخفاها وحقرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r10.claim: A prophetic supplication asks God to grant the soul piety and purify it, supporting the reading in which God is the purifier.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r10.anchor: اللهم آت نفسي تقواها وزكها أنت خير من زكاها أنت وليها ومولاها

AKHFASH:v2p580/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p580/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p580/r1.claim: Mā in wa-nafsin wa-mā sawwāhā means the One who fashioned it; God swears by Himself as Lord of the soul He formed, and the oath's answer is qad aflaḥa man zakkāhā.
AKHFASH:v2p580/r1.anchor: فاقسم الله تبارك وتعالى بنفسه وانه رب النفس التي سواها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says this clause answers the oath; the lām is omitted because the extended wording compensates for it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج هذا جواب القسم والمعنى لقد أفلح ولكن اللام حذفت لأن الكلام طال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the oath's answer is omitted.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل والفراء والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r3.claim: One interpretation says the soul God purified has succeeded.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r3.anchor: أحدهما قد أفلحت نفس زكاها الله عز وجل قاله ابن عباس ومقاتل والفراء والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r4.speaker: قتادة وابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r4.claim: A second interpretation says the one who purifies himself through obedience and righteous deeds has succeeded.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r4.anchor: والثاني قد أفلح من زكى نفسه بطاعة الله وصالح الأعمال قاله قتادة وابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r5.claim: Zakkāhā means to repair the soul and purify it of sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p141/r5.anchor: ومعنى زكاها أصلحها وطهرها من الذنوب

IBNKATHIR:91:9/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r7.claim: One reading is that a person succeeds by purifying himself through obedience to God and cleansing base traits; Qatada says this directly, with similar reports from Mujahid, ʿIkrima, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and 87:14–15 is a parallel.
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r7.anchor: أي : بطاعة الله - كما قال قتادة - وطهرها من الأخلاق الدنيئة والرذائل .

IBNKATHIR:91:9/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r9.claim: A second possible reading, attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas by al-ʿAwfi and ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, is that God purifies the successful soul and debases the failed one.
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r9.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون المعنى : قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه ،   وقد خاب من دَسَّى الله نفسه

IBNKATHIR:91:9/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r10.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas says the Prophet interpreted the verse as a soul that God purifies; Ibn Kathir notes Juwaybir is abandoned in hadith and al-Dahhak never met Ibn ʿAbbas.
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r10.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " أفلحت نفس زكاها الله " {[30137]} .   ورواه ابن أبي حاتم

IBNKATHIR:91:9/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r11.claim: Al-Tabarani reports that when the Prophet reached these verses he paused and prayed for his soul's piety and purification; al-Haythami grades the chain hasan.
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r11.anchor: وقال الطبراني : حدثنا يحيى بن عثمان بن صالح ،   حدثنا أبي ،   حدثنا ابن لَهِيعة ،   عن عمرو بن دينار ،   عن ابن عباس قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا مر بهذه الآية :

IBNKATHIR:91:9/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r12.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet reciting the verse and praying that God give his soul piety and purify it; Ibn Kathir notes this route is not included by the major collectors.
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r12.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ : { فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا } قال :  " اللهم آت نفسي تقواها ،

IBNKATHIR:91:9/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r13.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r13.claim: ʿAisha found the Prophet missing from his bed and then encountered him prostrating while praying for his soul's piety and purification; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r13.anchor: عن عائشة : أنها فَقَدت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من مضجعه ،   فلمسته بيدها ،   فوقعت{[30141]}  عليه وهو ساجد ،

IBNKATHIR:91:9/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r14.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r14.claim: The Prophet taught Zayd ibn Arqam a prayer seeking refuge from several vices and asking God to give the soul piety and purify it; Muslim transmits the report.
IBNKATHIR:91:9/r14.anchor: عن زيد بن أرقم قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول :  " اللهم ،   إني أعوذ بك من العجز والكَسَل والهرم ،

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530/r1.claim: The successful person purifies himself through good works and acts of kindness.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530/r1.anchor: {قد أفلح من زكاها} أي من زكى نفسه بعمل [البر] ، واصطناع المعروف.

JISHUMI:v10p7431/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r2.speaker: الخليل
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r2.claim: Al-Khalīl says an implicit lām belongs with qad aflaḥ, yielding la-qad aflaḥa.
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r2.anchor: قال الخليل: اللام مضمر فيه، أي: لقد أفلح

JISHUMI:v10p7431/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r3.claim: Another grammatical account has fronting and postponement, estimating “successful is the one who purifies it,” ahead of the sun oath.
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r3.anchor: وقيل: بل فيه تقديم وتأخير، تقديره: قد أفلح من زكاها والشمس وضحاها

KASHSHAF:91:9/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:9/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:9/r1.claim: The person acts as agent of purification or debasement; purification grows and elevates through piety, while debasement diminishes and conceals through sin.

KASHSHAF:91:9/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:9/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:9/r2.claim: The root of dassaha is d-s-s, like the form cited for taqadada.
KASHSHAF:91:9/r2.anchor: وأصل دسى : دسس ،   كما قيل في تقضض

KASHSHAF:91:9/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:9/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF:91:9/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the wording by comparing it with purifying oneself in the cited verse and carrying wrongdoing in another.
KASHSHAF:91:9/r3.anchor: وسئل ابن عباس عنه فقال : أتقرأ :

KASHSHAF:91:9/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:9/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:9/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects the Qadari view that God is the subject of purification and debasement, condemning their attribution of an evil destiny to God.
KASHSHAF:91:9/r4.anchor: وأما قول من زعم أنّ الضمير في زكّى ودسى لله تعالى

KASHSHAF:91:9/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:9/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:9/r5.claim: The oath's omitted answer is that God will destroy the people of Mecca for denying Muhammad as He destroyed Thamud for denying Salih; the success saying is a tangent from the preceding verse, not the oath's answer.
KASHSHAF:91:9/r5.anchor: هو محذوف تقديره : ليدمدمنّ الله عليهم

KASHSHAF:91:10/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:10/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:10/r1.claim: The person acts as agent of purification or debasement; purification grows and elevates through piety, while debasement diminishes and conceals through sin.

KASHSHAF:91:10/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:10/r2.speaker: author

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r21.claim: He says the oath concludes here and counts eleven oaths in the passage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r21.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فيها أحد عشر قسما

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r22.claim: One reading says God purified the soul through obedience and good deeds.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r23.claim: Another reading says the person purified his own soul through obedience and good deeds.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r24.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r24.claim: He interprets zakkāhā as purified it.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r25.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r25.claim: He interprets zakkāhā as improved or reformed it.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r1.claim: “The successful one who purifies it” may be the answer to the oath, with an implied emphatic laam, as al-Zajjaj explains.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r1.anchor: جواب القسم والتقدير لقد أفلح قال الزجاج صار طول الكلام عوضا عن اللام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r2.claim: More plausibly, the oath's answer is omitted: God will destroy the Meccans for rejecting the Messenger as He destroyed Thamud for rejecting Salih; the purification statement is an aside extending the preceding verse.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r2.anchor: وقيل الجواب محذوف وهو الاظهر تقديره ليدمدمن من الله عليهم أى على أهل مكة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r3.claim: Purification means God cleansed, set right, and made the soul pure.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ من زكاها ﴾ طهرها الله وأصلحها وجعلها زاكية

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r1.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the oath’s lām is omitted because the intervening speech is long enough to substitute for it.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: اللام حذفت، لأن الكلام طال، فصار طوله عوضا منها

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r2.claim: Another analysis omits the oath’s answer: “by the sun and so on, you will surely be resurrected.”
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r2.anchor: وقيل: الجواب محذوف أي والشمس وكذا وكذا لتبعثن

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari infers that God will destroy Meccans for denying Muhammad as He destroyed Thamud for denying Salih; verses 9–10 are an aside, not the oath’s answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.anchor: الزمخشري: تقديره ليدمدمن الله عليهم أي على أهل مكة، لتكذيبهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، كما دمدم على ثمود لأنهم كذبوا صالحا

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r4.claim: Another view puts the successful/pitiable statements before the oath by inversion, without ellipsis.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو على التقديم والتأخير بغير حذف

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r6.claim: One reading says God purifies the soul through obedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r6.anchor: أي من زكى الله نفسه بالطاعة

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r8.claim: Qatada and others say a person succeeds by purifying himself with obedience and good deeds, and fails by hiding himself in sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r8.anchor: وقيل: أفلح من زكى نفسه بطاعة الله، وصالح الأعمال، وخاب من دس نفسه في المعاصي قاله قتادة وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r9.claim: Zakat originally means growth or increase; a judge’s endorsement of a witness likewise raises and praises him, discussed at the start of al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r9.anchor: وأصل الزكاة: النمو والزيادة، ومنه زكا الزرع: إذا كثر ريعه

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r10.claim: Generous Arabs settled on high ground and lit fires for visitors; stingy people hid in hollows, just as virtue raises and sin conceals a person.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r10.anchor: فمصطنع المعروف والمبادر إلى أعمال البر، شهر نفسه ورفعها. وكانت أجواد العرب تنزل الربا وارتفاع الأرض

QUTB-ZILAL:91:9/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:9/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:9/r1.claim: Alongside innate dispositions, each person has a conscious, discerning, directing faculty; that faculty bears responsibility.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:9/r1.anchor: إلى جانب هذه الاستعدادات الفطرية الكامنة قوة واعية مدركة موجهة في ذات الإنسان

QUTB-ZILAL:91:9/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:9/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:9/r2.claim: A person flourishes by using this faculty to purify the self, develop its capacity for good, and make good prevail over evil.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:9/r2.anchor: فمن استخدم هذه القوة في تزكية نفسه وتطهيرها وتنمية استعداد الخير فيها

RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعطاء وعكرمة ومقاتل والكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, ʿAta, ʿIkrima, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi interpret the successful soul as one God purified and enabled to obey.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175/r6.anchor: المروي عن سعيد بن جبير وعطاء وعكرمة ومقاتل والكلبي

RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r1.claim: Tazkiya means purification or growth; one reading says a person succeeds by purifying the soul through obedience and avoiding sin.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r1.anchor: فاعلم أن التزكية عبارة عن التطهير أو عن الإنماء

RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r2.claim: The Qadi accepts the alternative that God purifies the soul by judging or naming it pure, while saying the self-purifying reading is closer because nafs is the explicit antecedent.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r2.anchor: وقبل القاضي هذا التأويل ، وقال المراد منه أن الله حكم بتزكيتها

RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r3.claim: Razi rejects the naming interpretation: verbal forms indicate bringing about, and an unchangeable divine judgment cannot change from truth to falsehood or knowledge to ignorance.

RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r4.claim: Razi argues that the nearest antecedent is 'inspired it,' closer to mā than 'a soul,' so grammar supports his interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r4.anchor: فإن أهل اللغة اتفقوا على أن عود الضمير إلى الأقرب

RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r5.speaker: سعيد بن أبي هلال
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi reports from Saʿid ibn Abi Hilal that the Prophet paused at this verse and prayed for his soul's piety and purification, naming God as its guardian.
RAZI-FULL:v31p175#3/r5.anchor: ما رواه الواحدي في البسيط عن سعيد بن أبي هلال

RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r8.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi says God swears by the noblest creatures to the success of the soul He purifies and the loss of the one He abandons, precluding self-directed purification or ruin outside prior decree.
RAZI-FULL:v31p176/r8.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : فكأنه سبحانه أقسم بأشرف مخلوقاته

STUDYQURAN:91:9/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r1.claim: These verses inspired extensive writing on purification of the soul, regarded by some as the Quran's entire purpose.
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r1.anchor: These two verses have served as the inspiration for extensive literature on the “purification of the soul”

STUDYQURAN:91:9/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r2.speaker: Bg, Sh
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r2.claim: Most take verse 9 to begin the answer to the oaths in verses 1–7; others say the answer is omitted and implied.
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r2.anchor: Most take v. 9 to be the beginning of the answer to the oaths taken in vv. 1–7

STUDYQURAN:91:9/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r3.claim: The verses describe cleansing lowly traits and, conversely, dulling the soul through heedlessness and disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r3.anchor: The text speaks of those who cleanse the soul of lowly and despicable character traits

STUDYQURAN:91:9/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r4.speaker: IK, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r4.claim: Some early commentators make God the subject: the soul God purifies prospers, and the soul He obscures fails.
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r4.anchor: According to some of the earliest commentators, these two verses could also be read with God as the subject

STUDYQURAN:91:9/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r5.claim: The subject's ambiguity can express cooperation between God and people: people purify themselves for their own souls while willing only as God wills; God purifies whom He will, yet changes a people when they change themselves.
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r5.anchor: The ambiguity of the subject can also be seen as an allusion to the cooperation between God and human beings

STUDYQURAN:91:9/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r6.speaker: Sh, Z
STUDYQURAN:91:9/r6.claim: The literal meanings are to grow for purify and to bury for obscure; the verses can be rendered whoever grows the soul prospers, whoever buries it fails.

SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r1.claim: Qad aflaḥa may be the oath's answer, originally la-qad, with lām dropped because the intervening wording is long.
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r1.anchor: أنه جواب القسم، والأصل: لقد، وإنما حذفت لطول الكلام

SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r2.claim: Alternatively, qad aflaḥa is a digression after the inspiration clause, not the oath's answer; the omitted answer predicts God's destruction of Meccans for denying the Messenger as Thamūd denied Ṣāliḥ.
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r2.anchor: فالجواب محذوف تقديره: ليدمدمن الله عليهم، أي: على أهل مكة لتكذيبهم رسول الله

SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r3.claim: Another proposed omitted oath answer is that the people will surely be resurrected.
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r3.anchor: قال معناه الزمخشري، وقدره غيره: لتبعثن.

SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r6.claim: The apparent subject of zakāhā and dassāhā is man; an alternative makes God the subject, but the author rejects it as syntactically awkward because the pronoun must refer back through nafs and its possessor.
SAMIN-DURR:91:8-9/r6.anchor: والحق أنه خلاف الظاهر، لا لما قال الزمخشري، بل لمنافرة نظمه للاحتياج إلى عود الضمير على النفس

TAB-FULL:v24p444/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r1.claim: Success belongs to the person whose soul God purifies from disbelief and sins and reforms through righteous deeds.
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r1.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، {قد أفلح من زكاها} [الشمس: 9] يقول: قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه

TAB-FULL:v24p444/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses purification as God purifying the person's soul.
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r2.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، {قد أفلح من زكاها} [الشمس: 9] يقول: قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه

TAB-FULL:v24p444/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r3.speaker: مجاهد، سعيد بن جبير، عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r3.claim: Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and ʿIkrima explain the phrase as whoever reforms the soul.
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r3.anchor: عن خصيف، عن مجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، وعكرمة: {قد أفلح من زكاها} [الشمس: 9] قالوا: من أصلحها

TAB-FULL:v24p444/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r4.claim: Qatāda says a person purifies the soul by doing good in obedience to God.
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {قد أفلح من زكاها} [الشمس: 9] : من عمل خيرا زكاها بطاعة الله

TAB-FULL:v24p444/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd also interprets success as God purifying the person's soul.
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {قد أفلح من زكاها} [الشمس: 9] يقول: قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه

TAB-FULL:v24p444/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r6.claim: Qatāda identifies this clause as the point where the oath's answer occurs.
TAB-FULL:v24p444/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: قد وقع القسم هاهنا {قد أفلح من زكاها} [الشمس: 9]

TABATABAI:91:9-10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r7.claim: Success means attaining one’s goal and failure its opposite. Tazkiya evokes blessed plant-growth, while tadsiya means covertly inserting or corrupting something, here deforming the soul’s proper growth.
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r7.anchor: والتزكية إنماؤه كذلك، والتدسي - وهو من الدس بقلب إحدى السينين ياء - إدخال الشيء في الشيء بضرب من الإخفاء

TABATABAI:91:9-10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r8.claim: These verses answer the oath and describe reform or corruption of the soul: innate recognition of piety makes submission to God natural, and taqwā cultivates it and supplies its lasting provision.
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r8.anchor: والتعبير بالتزكية والتدسي عن إصلاح النفس وإفسادها مبتن على ما يدل عليه قوله { فألهمها فجورها وتقواها }

TABATABAI:91:11-15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r1.claim: Taqwā is the best provision for the soul’s lasting life, as the Qurʾān tells people to provision themselves with piety.
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r1.anchor: وتزودوا فإن خير الزاد التقوى واتقون يا أولي الألباب

ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r3.claim: Aflaha describes the soul God purified; another view makes it a person who purifies himself by righteous deeds.
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r3.anchor: أي قد أفلحت نفس زكاها الله.

THALABI:v10p213/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p213/r1.claim: The oath reaches its answer here: the soul God purifies succeeds and is made able to fear Him.
THALABI:v10p213/r1.anchor: قد أفلح سعد وفاز، وهاهنا موضع القسم. من زكاها أي أفلحت نفس زكاها الله

THALABI:v10p213/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
THALABI:v10p213/r4.claim: One glosses purification as reforming the soul, and the other as purifying it.
THALABI:v10p213/r4.anchor:
عن سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد:
قد أفلح من زكاها قال: أحدها أصلحها، وقال الآخر: طهرها

THALABI:v10p213/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
THALABI:v10p213/r8.claim: A soul succeeds when God purifies it and fails when God corrupts it.
THALABI:v10p213/r8.anchor: قد أفلحت نفس زكاها الله، وخابت نفس أفسدها الله عز وجل

THALABI:v10p213/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r9.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p213/r9.claim: A person may purify and reform the soul by making it obey God, or ruin it by leading it into disobedience.
THALABI:v10p213/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه قد أفلح من زكى نفسه فأصلحها وحملها على طاعة الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p56/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p56/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، الكلبي، مجاهد، عكرمة، سعيد بن جبير، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p56/r1.claim: The successful soul is one God has purified and set right, enabling it to obey and then act in obedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p56/r1.anchor:
قد أفلحت نفس زكاها الله وأصلحها، وهو قول:
مجاهد (¬1)، وعكرمة

WAHIDI-QT:91:9/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:91:9/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:91:9/r1.claim: The successful person is happy, and God has repaired and purified that person's self from sins.
WAHIDI-QT:91:9/r1.anchor: { قد أفلح } سعد { من زكاها } أصلح الله نفسه وطهرها من الذنوب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r1.claim: The one who succeeds is made happy, as God reforms his soul and purifies it from sins.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r1.anchor: سعد { من زكاها } أصلح الله نفسه وطهرها من الذنوب.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r14.claim: The person who cleans a soul from sin and nurtures it through taqwa truly succeeds and reaches the promised divine welcome and Paradise; alternatively, the successful soul is one God purifies.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r14.anchor: yani fücurdan temizleyip takvâ ile terbiye ve tenmiye ederek feyizlendiren kimseler

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r16.claim: Most commentators take these two statements as the oath's answer; the lam of laqad is omitted because the oath is long, and the pair summarizes the surah's purpose.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r16.anchor: Ekser müfessirînin beyânına göre kasemlerin cevâbı bu iki cümledir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r17.claim: Zakā/teziya derives from the root behind zakat and means purity together with growth, increase, and blessing.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r17.anchor: Bu ise “arılık”[^15] dediğimiz temizlik, paklık, tahâret mânasıyla artıp büyümek demek olan “nemâ”, feyz u bereket mânasınadır.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r18.claim: The first sense of purifying the soul is cleansing it of disbelief, ignorance, bad feelings, false beliefs, and bad character.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r18.anchor: onu kirletecek küfür, cehalet, kötü hisler, yanlış itikadlar, fena ahlâklar gibi fücurdan temizlemek.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r19.claim: The second sense is preserving and cultivating faith, knowledge, benevolence, and divine character so the soul receives divine manifestations and spreads good and blessing; this is the apparent sense and a duty and benefit.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r19.anchor: iman, ilm ü irfan, iyi, hayırhâh hisler, güzel, ilâhî ahlâk gibi takvâ hasletleriyle terbiye edip ilâhî tecelliyâta mazhar

ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r20.claim: Purification can be attributed to a person through acquisition, to mentors through causation, and to God through decree, success, and creation.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#2/r20.anchor: kesbi itibariyle insana ve sebebiyeti itibariyle mürşid ve muallim gibi âharîne ve takdîr u tevfik ve halkı itibariyle Allah’a nisbet olunur.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r1.claim: A third sense is certifying or praising a soul as pure and fully grown; people may not commend themselves this way before knowing their fate, as al-Najm forbids.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r1.anchor: nefsin temizliğini takdir veya son derece feyz ü nemâsına ermiş olduğuna hükmetmek suretiyle temize çıkarmak, övmek mânasına gelir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r2.claim: On the self-purification reading, man is the human agent and the pronoun in it refers to the soul; on the divine reading, the soul is the one God purifies.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r2.anchor: “Allah’ın tezkiye ettiği nefis felah buldu” diye anlamak lâzım gelir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r3.claim: The Mu'tazila insist on reading the person as purifying the soul, while Sunnis allow the alternative that God purifies it and regard attribution to God as truer.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r3.anchor: Mu‘tezile bu mânada ısrar etmek istemişlerse de Ehl-i Sünnet ikinci vechi de tecviz etmişler

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r4.claim: Both grammatical readings are possible, so Elmalılı's translation leaves them open and his commentary explains each.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r4.anchor: mealde iki veche de muhtemil bir surette ifade edilmiş, tefsirde iki vecih dahi gösterilmiştir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r5.claim: A person is responsible for striving to purify the soul for its own benefit; exercising will in God's service brings God's help.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r5.anchor: insanın nefsini, rûhunu tezkiyeye çalışması sonunda menfaati kendine ait olan bir vazifesidir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r6.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r6.claim: The Prophet prayed that God grant his soul taqwa and purify it, since God is the best purifier and its guardian and master.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r6.anchor: اَللّٰهُمَّ آتِ نـَفْسِي تـَقْوَاهَا وَزَكِّهَا أَنْتَ خَيـْرُ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r7.claim: Tabarani and others report from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet would pause after reciting this verse and say the purification prayer.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r7.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm bu âyeti tilâvet eylediği zaman vakfeder ve bu duayı söylerdi.

ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r8.claim: Some prefer the divine-agent reading because related hadiths and parallel verbs let their agents consistently refer to God; Elmalılı prefers human responsibility as the passage's focus, while the Prophet's prayer is itself human striving.
ELMALILI:91:5-10#3/r8.anchor: asıl mesele insanın kendisi hakkında kendi kesbiyle mes’ûliyetini anlatmak olduğu cihetle evvelki vecih daha müfiddir.

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r1.claim: The blessing formula recalls Psalm 1:1 and especially 87:14, another blessing using aflaḥa and a z-k-w/y verb; other related Quranic usages are noted.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Die Formel qad ʾaflaḥa man erinnert an das psalmische

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r2.claim: Arabic zakā originally means ‘grow, flourish’; the Quranic moral sense of purity most likely reflects semantic convergence with Aramaic dḵā, unlike the Arabic root ṭ-h-r for ritual purity.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Zakā bedeutet im Arabischen ursprünglich „wachsen, gedeihen“; die koranische Bedeutung der Wurzel, die primär die Vorstellung moralischer Reinheit ausdrückt

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Torrey
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r3.claim: Torrey attributes the semantic convergence between Arabic z-k-w/y and its Aramaic homonym to Jewish usage; Andrae adduces Syriac literary parallels.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Torrey nimmt an, dass der Bedeutungsangleichung von arab. z-k-w/y an sein aramäisches Homonym jüdischer Sprachgebrauch zugrunde liege

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r4.claim: The shift likely predates the Quran and arose through cultural contact with Aramaic speakers, as Bell argues for semantically Aramaic-influenced terms such as ṣallā.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Wahrscheinlicher ist vielmehr, dass sie bereits in vorkoranischer Zeit im Zuge des kulturellen Kontakts mit der aramäischsprachigen Bevölkerung des Fruchtbaren Halbmonds stattfand (so Bell 1926, 51)

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r5.speaker: Horovitz
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r5.claim: Horovitz treats even the earliest Quranic z-k-w/y verbs as specialized forms meaning to give alms; Schulthess accordingly translates this verse as making a good afterlife bargain by almsgiving.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r5.anchor: Horovitz etwa versteht bereits die frühesten koranischen Vorkommnisse der Wurzel im spezialisierten Sinn von „Almosen geben“

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r6.claim: The author reads zakkā in 91:9 as the soul’s moral purification, not almsgiving; this general sense also fits early 80:3, 80:7, and 87:14.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r6.anchor: vor allem in 91:9 bezeichnet zakkā ganz unzweifelhaft die moralische „Läuterung“ der Seele

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r7.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r7.claim: Neuwirth points to 92:18, where giving one’s wealth is linked to yatazakkā, as possible evidence for almsgiving, but the author finds that interpretation no more compelling than moral purification.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r7.anchor: so Neuwirth, Frühmekkanische Suren, 221, was jedoch nicht mit der von ihr ebd., 227 gewählten Übersetzung harmoniert

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r8.claim: The link between spending wealth and tazakkā in 92:18 is a step toward the verb’s later narrowing to almsgiving, though its broader sense remains fitting there.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9:anmerkung/r8.anchor: Doch stellt die enge Verknüpfung von tazakkā mit dem Spenden von Besitz in 92:18

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.claim: The oath’s list of opposing created phenomena moves into morality in verses 7–8 and ends with a contrastive oath naming the opposed outcomes of those moral choices.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die Liste gegensätzlicher Schöpfungsphänomene, die in V. 7.8 in den Bereich des Moralischen übergeht, endet schließlich mit einer ebenfalls kontrastiv gegliederte Schwuraussage

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r2.claim: The feminine suffix -hā in verses 9–10 refers syntactically back to the soul in verse 7.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r2.anchor: Der enge sachliche Zusammenhang der Schwuraussage mit dem letzten Schwurelement, der Seele, zeigt sich dabei auch syntaktisch in dem pronominalen Rückbezug des femininen Suffixes -hā auf die nafs aus V. 7.

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r3.claim: Although other early suras frame conduct and outcome eschatologically, this sura does not explicitly mention afterlife recompense; ashqā in verse 12 may carry such connotations.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r3.anchor: die vorliegende Sure nicht ausdrücklich auf eine jenseitige Vergeltung; allerdings dürfte der Gebrauch des Ausdrucks ʾašqā in V. 12 eschatologische Konnotationen transportiert haben

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#3/r1.claim: Qatāda says the successful person purifies himself through good action, while the failed person buries himself in sin and wrongdoing.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p376#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ قد أفلح من زكاها ﴾ قال قد أفلح من زكى نفسه بعمل صالح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r5.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj and others take “successful is whoever purifies it” as the oath’s answer, with an omitted emphatic lām after the long intervening text.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r5.anchor: قد أفلح من زكاها، قال الزجاج وغيره: هذا جواب القسم، وحذفت اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī instead supplies “God will destroy them”—the Meccans for denying Muḥammad as Thamūd denied Ṣāliḥ—and treats purification as a digression, not the oath’s answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: تقديره ليدمدمن الله عليهم، أي على أهل مكة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r7.claim: Purification is the soul’s growth and emergence through good works; corruption hides and diminishes it through sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489/r7.anchor: وزكاؤها: ظهورها ونماؤها بالعمل الصالح، ودساها: أخفاها وحقرها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.claim: The preceding surah ended with the people of the right and left; this one summarizes the two groups in the successful purifier and failed corrupter, and its inspiration verse can explain the two paths in the previous surah.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p139#4/r8.anchor: ولما ختم سبحانه السورة المتقدمة بذكر أصحاب الميمنة وأصحاب المشأمة أعاد جل شأنه في هذه السورة الفريقين على سبيل الفذلكة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#2/r1.claim: Qatāda, al-Zajjāj, and others take this as the answer to the oath; omission of the expected laam is common, especially where it eases a long construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#2/r1.anchor: جواب القسم على ما أخرجه الجماعة عن قتادة وإليه ذهب الزجاج وغيره وحذف اللام كثير لا سيما عند الكلام المقتضي للتخفيف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#2/r2.claim: The subject of زكاها is the person who purifies, and its object pronoun refers to the soul; the same construction applies to the next verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#2/r2.anchor: وفاعل زكاها ضمير من والضمير المنصوب للنفس وكذا في

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses purification as growth and elevation, and concealment as diminishment and hiding: piety raises the soul in knowledge and action, while sin hides and diminishes it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r3.anchor: وفي الكشاف التزكية الإنماء والإعلاء والتدسية النقص والإخفاء أي لقد فاز بكل مطلوب ونجا من كل مكروه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes purification cleansing the soul from material stain and concealment hiding or entangling it in that matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r4.anchor: وجوز أن تفسر التزكية بالتطهير من دنس الهيولي والتدسية بالإخفاء فيه والتلوث به

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r5.claim: The oath and paired promise and warning display God's knowledge, necessary existence, perfect attributes, and abundant gracious gifts to His servants.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143#3/r5.anchor: ففي الوعد والوعيد المذكورين مع إقسامه تعالى عليهما بما أقسم به مما يدل على العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the purification statements as a parenthesis and makes the oath's omitted answer a threat to destroy Meccan disbelievers as Thamūd were destroyed for rejecting Ṣāliḥ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري قوله تعالى قد أفلح الخ تابعا لقوله تعالى فألهمها الخ على سبيل الأستطراد وأبى أن يكون جواب القسم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.claim: Alusi objects that omitting the laam is far more common and less cumbersome than omitting an entire clause; purification is itself a central aim, not merely a practical-intellect concern or disposable preliminary.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.anchor: وتعقب بأن حذف اللام كثير لاسيما مع الطول وهو أسهل من حذف الجملة بتمامها وقد ذكره في قد أفلح المؤمنون

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r7.claim: The decree does not erase a role for human capacity and choice; assigning purification and concealment to people requires only their involvement, not that they independently create their acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r7.anchor: ولا يقتضي ذلك أن لا يكون لقدرة العبد واختياره مدخل في الفجور والتقوى بالكلية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r8.claim: Grammatical attribution to a person establishes involvement, not independent creation or autonomous power to choose and produce either state.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r8.anchor: لأن الإسناد يقتضي قيام المسند ويكفي فيه المدخلية المذكورة ولا يتوقف صحة الإسناد حقيقة إلى العبد على كون فعله الإيجاد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the successful person as one whose soul God purifies and guides, and the failed one as one whose soul God corrupts and misguides.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r1.anchor: قال في ذلك يقول الله تعالى قد أفلح من زكى الله تعالى نفسه فهداه وقد خاب من دسى الله تعالى نفسه فأضله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r2.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r2.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says a soul succeeds when God purifies it and fails when God deprives it of every good.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r2.anchor: أنه قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يقول في قوله تعالى قد أفلح من زكاها الآية أفلحت نفس زكاها الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r3.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Arqam reports the Prophet's prayer asking God to grant his soul piety and purify it, since God is the best purifier and its guardian.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن أرقم قال كان رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يقول اللهم آت نفسي تقواها وزكها أنت خير من زكاها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī's report from Ibn ʿAbbās says that when the Prophet recited the verse, he paused and prayed in this manner.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r4.anchor: وفي رواية الطبراني وغيره عن ابن عباس أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام إذا تلا الآية وقف وقال ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.speaker: صاحب الانتصاف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.claim: Some commentators and Ṣāḥib al-Intiṣāf prefer God as the subject of both verbs, citing these reports, consistent subjects throughout the oath, and the parallel passive-reflexive تزكى.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r5.anchor: ولهذه الأخبار ونحوها قال بعضهم أن ذلك هو المرجح ورجحه صاحب الانتصاف بأن الضمائر في السماء وما بناها الخ تكون عليه متسقة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.claim: Alusi says the human subject is still the first sense to occur to the mind, and the reports do not decisively establish the alternative; they do refute al-Zamakhsharī's charge that this is Sunnī reversal of the Qadarite position.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r6.anchor: ومع هذا كله لا ينبغي أن ينكر أن المعنى هو السابق إلى الذهن وما ذكر من الأخبار ليس نصا في تعيين المعنى الآخر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r1.claim: This is the oath’s answer: a soul succeeds when God reforms and cleans it of sin and enables it to obey.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r1.anchor: وهذا موضع القسم، أي فازت وسعدت نفس زكاها الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan instead makes the person the subject: one succeeds by purifying and directing the soul to obedience, and loses by ruining it through sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه قد أفلح من زكى نفسه فأصلحها وحملها على طاعة الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r5.claim: Zayd b. Arqam reports that the Prophet sought refuge from incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, worry, and grave punishment, asking God to grant and purify the soul’s piety and protect from other spiritual failings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r5.anchor: عن زيد بن أرقم قال: لا أقول لكم إلا ما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لنا: "اللهم إني أعوذ بك

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r1.claim: The success clause answers the oath; its lām is omitted for length. The oaths exhort people to perfect the soul through knowledge of the Creator and gratitude for His favors.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r1.anchor: أنماها بالعلم والعمل جواب القسم، وحذف اللام للطول

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r2.claim: Alternatively, the oath passage digresses on the soul and its answer is omitted: God would destroy Mecca's unbelievers as He destroyed Thamūd for rejecting Ṣāliḥ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r2.anchor: وقيل هو استطراد بذكر بعض أحوال النفس، والجواب محذوف تقديره ليدمدمن الله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r1.claim: The one who purifies the soul succeeds in attaining all aims by growing, reforming, and cleansing it through beneficial knowledge and good works.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r1.anchor: أي نماها وأصلحها وصفاها تصفية عظيمة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r2.claim: The verb zakkā can denote both growth and purification, matching the religious pattern of adorning virtues and removing vices.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r2.anchor: والدين بني على التحلية والتخلية و ( زكى ) صالح للمعنيين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r1.claim: The following Sūrat al-Layl shares al-Shams's theme: God has complete power and choice, shown by people's different paths despite shared aims in sensual pleasures and comfort.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r2.claim: Night's darkness and sleep, the sibling of death, frustrate many human desires and bring about opposing outcomes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445/r2.anchor: ليل نفسه دال على ذلك لأنه على غير مراد النفس بما فيه من الظلام

DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.claim: He says purification means improving the soul, concealment means leading it astray, Thamud denied through disobedience, and God does not fear their aftermath.
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.anchor: قال: عرفها شقاءها {قد أفلح من زكاها} قال: أصلحها {وقد خاب من دساها} قال: أغواها

DURR-FULL:v8p529/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r6.claim: He says the oath's answer occurs at ‘successful is whoever purifies it,’ and purification is doing good through obedience to God.
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r6.anchor: قال: وقع القسم ههنا {من زكاها} قال: من عمل خيرا فزكاها بطاعة الله

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r12.speaker: الكلبي
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r12.claim: He says God purifies the soul of the successful and darkens the soul of the failed.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r12.anchor: عن الكلبي {قد أفلح من زكاها} الآية قال: أفلح من زكاه الله وخاب من دساه الله

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r13.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r13.claim: He says success is purifying and reforming oneself, while failure is ruining and misleading oneself.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r13.anchor: عن الحسن في الآية: قد أفلح من زكى نفسه وأصلحها وخاب من أهلكها وأضلها

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r14.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r14.claim: He connects purifying the soul to righteous work and concealing it to evil work.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r14.anchor: عن الربيع في الآية يقول: أفلح من زكى نفسه بالعمل الصالح وخاب من دس نفسه بالعمل السيء

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r16.claim: He says God purifies the successful soul and darkens and misguides the failed one.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r16.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {قد أفلح من زكاها} يقول: قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه

DURR-FULL:v8p531/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says a soul prospers when God purifies it and fails when God deprives it of every good.
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: {قد أفلح من زكاها} الآية

ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r1.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj and others say this is the oath's answer; the lām is omitted because the statement is long, with laqad aflaha understood.
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج وغيره : هذا جواب القسم

ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r2.claim: Another view says the oath's answer is omitted and estimates it as la-tubʿathunna, you will surely be resurrected.

ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī estimates the answer as God's destruction of Mecca's people for rejecting His Messenger, as He destroyed Thamūd for rejecting Ṣāliḥ; he treats this verse as an aside.
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : تقديره ليدمدمن الله عليهم

ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r4.claim: Purification means the soul's emergence and growth through righteous deeds; concealment hides and degrades it through sins.

ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r5.speaker: الحسن وغيره
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r5.claim: The apparent agent of both verbs is the pronoun referring back to man.
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن فاعل زكى ودسى ضمير يعود على من ،   وقاله الحسن

ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās allows the pronoun to refer to God, with feminine agreement because man is understood as soul.
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r6.anchor: وقائل ذلك هو بحر العلم عبد الله بن عباس

ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r7.speaker: رسول الله
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r7.claim: The Prophet would pray on reciting the verse: O God, grant my soul its piety and purify it; You are the best to purify it and its guardian and master.
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r7.anchor: كان عليه السلام إذا قرأ هذه الآية قال : « اللهم آت نفسي تقواها

ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī attacks the divine-agent reading as Qadarite blame of God.
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : وأما قول من زعم أن الضمير في زكى ودسى لله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says al-Zamakhsharī follows his habit of insulting Sunnis; Ibn ʿAbbās held the view, and the Prophet's supplication supports it.
ABUHAYYAN:91:9/r9.anchor: فجرى على عادته في سب أهل السنة . هذا ،   وقائل ذلك هو بحر العلم عبد الله بن عباس

ALUSI:91:9/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r1.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI:91:9/r1.claim: Qatāda, al-Zajjāj and others take verse 9 as the answer to the oath; its lām is omitted, especially after lengthy wording, for brevity or because the answer itself suffices.
ALUSI:91:9/r1.anchor: جواب القسم على ما أخرجه الجماعة عن قتادة وإليه ذهب الزجاج وغيره وحذف اللام كثير لاسيما عند طول الكلام

ALUSI:91:9/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r2.claim: The subject of each verb is the pronoun referring to من, while the suffix refers to the soul.
ALUSI:91:9/r2.anchor: وفاعل زكاها ضمير من والضمير المنصوب للنفس وكذا في قوله تعالى

ALUSI:91:9/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r4.claim: Tazkiya means growth, while tadsiyah means concealment.

ALUSI:91:9/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r8.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI:91:9/r8.claim: Al-Kashshāf glosses tazkiya as growth and elevation, and tadsiyah as diminution and concealment.
ALUSI:91:9/r8.anchor: التزكية الإنماء والإعلاء والتدسية النقص والإخفاء

ALUSI:91:9/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r9.claim: The successful person grows and elevates the soul through taqwā in knowledge and action; the loser diminishes and hides it through sin, ignorance and transgression.
ALUSI:91:9/r9.anchor: أي لقد فاز بكل مطلوب ونجا من كل مكروه من أنمى نفسه وأعلاها بالتقوى علماً وعملاً

ALUSI:91:9/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r10.claim: Another reading takes tazkiya as purification from the dross of matter and tadsiyah as hiding in and becoming polluted by it.
ALUSI:91:9/r10.anchor: وجوز أن تفسر التزكية بالتطهير من دنس الهيولى والتدسية بالإخفاء فيه والتلوث به

ALUSI:91:9/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:9/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:9/r11.claim: The promised success and threatened loss, sworn to by these signs, attest to God’s knowledge, necessary existence and perfect attributes, and display His beneficence toward servants.
ALUSI:91:9/r11.anchor: ففي الوعد والوعيد المذكورين مع إقسامه تعالى عليهما بما أقسم به مما يدل على العلم بوجوده تعالى ووجوب ذاته

ALUSI:91:10/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:10/r1.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI:91:10/r1.claim: Qatāda, al-Zajjāj and others take verse 9 as the answer to the oath; its lām is omitted, especially after lengthy wording, for brevity or because the answer itself suffices.
ALUSI:91:10/r1.anchor: جواب القسم على ما أخرجه الجماعة عن قتادة وإليه ذهب الزجاج وغيره وحذف اللام كثير لاسيما عند طول الكلام

ALUSI:91:10/r2.speaker: author

ALUSI:91:10/r2.anchor: وفاعل زكاها ضمير من والضمير المنصوب للنفس وكذا في قوله تعالى

ALUSI:91:10/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:10/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:10/r4.claim: Tazkiya means growth, while tadsiyah means concealment.

ALUSI:91:10/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:10/r8.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI:91:10/r8.claim: Al-Kashshāf glosses tazkiya as growth and elevation, and tadsiyah as diminution and concealment.
ALUSI:91:10/r8.anchor: التزكية الإنماء والإعلاء والتدسية النقص والإخفاء

ALUSI:91:10/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:10/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:10/r9.claim: The successful person grows and elevates the soul through taqwā in knowledge and action; the loser diminishes and hides it through sin, ignorance and transgression.
ALUSI:91:10/r9.anchor: أي لقد فاز بكل مطلوب ونجا من كل مكروه من أنمى نفسه وأعلاها بالتقوى علماً وعملاً

ALUSI:91:10/r10.speaker: author
