ALUSI:91:10/r10.anchor: وجوز أن تفسر التزكية بالتطهير من دنس الهيولى والتدسية بالإخفاء فيه والتلوث به

ALUSI:91:10/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:10/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:10/r11.claim: The promised success and threatened loss, sworn to by these signs, attest to God’s knowledge, necessary existence and perfect attributes, and display His beneficence toward servants.
ALUSI:91:10/r11.anchor: ففي الوعد والوعيد المذكورين مع إقسامه تعالى عليهما بما أقسم به مما يدل على العلم بوجوده تعالى ووجوب ذاته

BAGHAWI:91:9/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:9/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:91:9/r1.claim: This is the object of the oath: the soul God purifies succeeds and is happy, for He repairs it, cleanses it of sins, and enables it to obey.
BAGHAWI:91:9/r1.anchor: وهذا موضع القسم ، أي فازت وسعدت نفس زكاها الله ، أي أصلحها وطهرها من الذنوب

BAGHAWI:91:10/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:10/r2.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI:91:10/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the successful person purifies and directs himself to obedience, while the failed person ruins and misleads himself toward sin; this reading makes the soul the agent of the verbs.
BAGHAWI:91:10/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن : معناه قد أفلح من زكى نفسه فأصلحها وحملها على طاعة الله عز وجل

BAGHAWI:91:10/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:10/r4.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
BAGHAWI:91:10/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Arqam transmits the Prophet's prayer seeking refuge from incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, senility, and the grave's punishment; it asks God to grant and purify the soul's piety, then seeks refuge from useless knowledge, an unsated soul, an unhumble heart, and unanswered supplication.
BAGHAWI:91:10/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن أرقم قال : " لا أقول لكم إلا ما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لنا : اللهم إني أعوذ بك

BAYDAWI:91:9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:91:9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:91:9/r1.claim: Whoever purifies the soul makes it grow through knowledge and action.
BAYDAWI:91:9/r1.anchor: قد أفلح من زكاها أنماها بالعلم والعمل جواب القسم

BAYDAWI:91:9/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:91:9/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:91:9/r2.claim: The verse answers the oath, with the lām omitted for length; the oath urges completion of the soul, appealing to knowledge of the Creator and gratitude for His favors as the highest theoretical and practical excellences.
BAYDAWI:91:9/r2.anchor: جواب القسم وحذف اللام للطول كأنه لما أراد به الحث على تكميل النفس والمبالغة فيه أقسم عليه بما يدلهم على العلم بوجود الصانع

BAYDAWI:91:9/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:91:9/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:91:9/r3.claim: Alternatively, the oath's answer is omitted: God will destroy Meccan disbelievers for rejecting Muhammad as He destroyed Thamūd for rejecting Ṣāliḥ.
BAYDAWI:91:9/r3.anchor: وقيل هو استطراد بذكر بعض أحوال النفس والجواب محذوف تقديره ليدمدمن الله على كفار مكة لتكذيبهم رسول

BIQAI:91:9/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:9/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:9/r1.claim: Success means attaining all one seeks; the successful person grows, reforms, and purifies the soul through beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds, removing blameworthy traits. The verb covers both adornment and cleansing, the paired foundations of religion.
BIQAI:91:9/r1.anchor: أي نماها وأصلحها وصفاها تصفية عظيمة بما يسره الله له من العلوم النافعة والأعمال الصالحة وطهرها

BIQAI:91:9/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:9/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:9/r2.claim: God makes each person able to pursue what that person was created for.
BIQAI:91:9/r2.anchor: لأن كلا ميسر لما خلق له

DURR:91:9/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r1.speaker: الكلبي
DURR:91:9/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says success is for the soul God purifies and failure for the soul God debases.
DURR:91:9/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي { قد أفلح من زكاها } الآية ، قال : أفلح من زكاه الله وخاب من دساه الله .

DURR:91:9/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR:91:9/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the successful person purifies and reforms the soul, while the loser destroys and misguides it.
DURR:91:9/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في الآية : قد أفلح من زكى نفسه وأصلحها ، وخاب من أهلكها وأضلها .

DURR:91:9/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r3.speaker: الربيع
DURR:91:9/r3.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the soul is purified through righteous deeds and debased through evil deeds.
DURR:91:9/r3.anchor: عن الربيع في الآية ، يقول : أفلح من زكى نفسه بالعمل الصالح ، وخاب من دس نفسه بالعمل السيئ .

DURR:91:9/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:91:9/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God purifies the successful soul and hides or debases the failed one, leading it astray; he adds that the one described does not fear anyone who follows him.
DURR:91:9/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { قد أفلح من زكاها } يقول : قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه

DURR:91:9/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:9/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:91:9/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through al-Dahhak attributes to the Prophet the saying that the soul God purifies succeeds, while the soul He deprives of all good fails.
DURR:91:9/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : { قد أفلح من زكاها }

DURR:91:10/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r1.speaker: الكلبي
DURR:91:10/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says success is for the soul God purifies and failure for the soul God debases.
DURR:91:10/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي { قد أفلح من زكاها } الآية ، قال : أفلح من زكاه الله وخاب من دساه الله .

DURR:91:10/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r2.speaker: الحسن

DURR:91:10/r2.anchor: عن الحسن في الآية : قد أفلح من زكى نفسه وأصلحها ، وخاب من أهلكها وأضلها .

DURR:91:10/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r3.speaker: الربيع
DURR:91:10/r3.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the soul is purified through righteous deeds and debased through evil deeds.
DURR:91:10/r3.anchor: عن الربيع في الآية ، يقول : أفلح من زكى نفسه بالعمل الصالح ، وخاب من دس نفسه بالعمل السيئ .

DURR:91:10/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:91:10/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God purifies the successful soul and hides or debases the failed one, leading it astray; he adds that the one described does not fear anyone who follows him.
DURR:91:10/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { قد أفلح من زكاها } يقول : قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه

DURR:91:10/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:10/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:91:10/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through al-Dahhak attributes to the Prophet the saying that the soul God purifies succeeds, while the soul He deprives of all good fails.
DURR:91:10/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : { قد أفلح من زكاها }

IBNATIYYA:91:9/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r1.claim: The oath's answer is qad aflaḥa, with an implied emphatic lām: la-qad aflaḥa.
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r1.anchor: وجواب القسم في قوله { قد أفلح } ، التقدير : لقد أفلح

IBNATIYYA:91:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others take God as the subject of purification: the group God purifies succeeds; man min can denote a group or an individual.
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r2.anchor: والفاعل ب «زكى » يحتمل أن يكون الله تعالى ، وقاله ابن عباس وغيره كأنه قال : قد أفلحت الفرقة أو الطائفة التي زكاها الله تعالى ، و { من } : تقع على جمع وإفراد

IBNATIYYA:91:9/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan and others take the human being as the subject: whoever acquires the purification God created for him succeeds.
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الفاعل ب «زكى » الإنسان ، وعليه تقع { من } وقاله الحسن وغيره ، كأنه قال : { قد أفلح } من زكى نفسه أي اكتسب الزكاء الذي قد خلقه الله

IBNATIYYA:91:9/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r4.claim: Zakkāhā means to purify the soul and make it grow through good deeds.
IBNATIYYA:91:9/r4.anchor: و { زكاها } معناه : طهرها ونماها بالخيرات

MAWARDI:91:9/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:9/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:91:9/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās counts eleven oaths in the preceding oath passage, whose answer is this statement of success.
MAWARDI:91:9/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فيها أحد عشر قسما

MAWARDI:91:9/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:9/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:91:9/r2.claim: One reading is that God purifies a person through obedience to Him and righteous deeds.
MAWARDI:91:9/r2.anchor: قد أفلح من زكى الله نفسه بطاعة الله وصالح الأعمال

MAWARDI:91:9/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:9/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:91:9/r3.claim: Another reading is that the person purifies their own soul through obedience and righteous deeds.
MAWARDI:91:9/r3.anchor: قد أفلح من زكى نفسه بطاعة الله وصالح الأعمال

MAWARDI:91:9/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:9/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI:91:9/r5.anchor: الثاني : أصلحها ، وهو قول سعيد بن جبير

NASAFI:91:9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:9/r1.claim: One analysis makes “qad aflaha” the answer to the oath; al-Zajjaj says the extended wording substitutes for the lām.
NASAFI:91:9/r1.anchor: { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ } جواب القسم والتقدير : لقد أفلح

NASAFI:91:9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:9/r2.claim: Nasafi calls it more evident that the answer is omitted—God will destroy the Meccans for rejecting Muhammad, as He destroyed Thamud for rejecting Salih.
NASAFI:91:9/r2.anchor: وقيل : الجواب محذوف وهو الأظهر تقديره ليدمدمن الله عليهم أي على أهل مكة لتكذيبهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI:91:9/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:9/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:9/r3.claim: On the preferred analysis, “qad aflaha” follows the prior phrase as an aside, not the oath's answer.
NASAFI:91:9/r3.anchor: وأما { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ } فكلام تابع لقوله { فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا } على سبيل الاستطراد

NASAFI:91:9/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:9/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:9/r4.claim: The one whose soul God purifies and makes righteous prospers.
NASAFI:91:9/r4.anchor: مَن زكاها } طهرها الله وأصلحها وجعلها زاكية

NASAFI:91:10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:10/r2.speaker: عكرمة
NASAFI:91:10/r2.claim: Ikrima says the soul purified by God prospers and the soul misled by God fails.
NASAFI:91:10/r2.anchor: قال عكرمة : أفلحت نفس زكاها الله وخابت نفس أغواها الله

NASAFI:91:10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:10/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:10/r3.claim: Alternatively, purifying and concealing the soul may be acts of the servant.
NASAFI:91:10/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون التدسية والتطهير فعل العبد

QURTUBI:91:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:9/r1.claim: This is the answer to the oath, with the sense لقد أفلح.
QURTUBI:91:9/r1.anchor: هذا جواب القسم ، بمعنى : لقد أفلح

QURTUBI:91:9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:9/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI:91:9/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the lām was omitted because the discourse is long enough to substitute for it.
QURTUBI:91:9/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : اللام حذفت ، لأن الكلام طال

QURTUBI:91:9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:9/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:91:9/r3.claim: Another view says the oath's response is omitted, with the implied sense that the hearers will surely be resurrected.
QURTUBI:91:9/r3.anchor: وقيل : الجواب محذوف ، أي والشمس وكذا وكذا لتبعثن

QURTUBI:91:9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:9/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI:91:9/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the missing oath response to mean God will destroy the Meccans for denying the Messenger, as He destroyed Thamūd for denying Ṣāliḥ; he treats this clause as an aside following the inspiration clause.

QURTUBI:91:9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:9/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI:91:9/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the successful one purifying the soul is an aside to God's inspiring it with wickedness and piety, not the oath's answer.
QURTUBI:91:9/r5.anchor: على سبيل الاستطراد ، وليس من جواب القسم في شيء

QURTUBI:91:9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:9/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:91:9/r6.claim: A further view uses fronting and postponement without ellipsis: the successful and failed souls are stated before the sun and its brightness.
QURTUBI:91:9/r6.anchor: وقيل : هو على التقديم والتأخير بغير حذف . والمعنى : قد أفلح من زكاها

QURTUBI:91:9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:9/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:9/r7.claim: Aflaḥa means to succeed or attain felicity.

QURTUBI:91:9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:9/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:9/r8.claim: The successful person is one whom God has purified through obedience.
QURTUBI:91:9/r8.anchor: " من زكاها " أي من زكى الله نفسه بالطاعة

RAZI:91:9/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:9/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:91:9/r1.anchor: التزكية عبارة عن التطهير أو عن الإنماء

RAZI:91:9/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:9/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:91:9/r2.claim: One view says the person succeeds by purifying their own soul from sins through obedience and avoiding disobedience.
RAZI:91:9/r2.anchor: أنه قد أدرك مطلوبه من زكى نفسه بأن طهرها من الذنوب بفعل الطاعة ومجانبة المعصية

RAZI:91:9/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:9/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:91:9/r3.claim: Al-Qāḍī accepts the alternative that God purifies the soul, taking this as God judging and naming it pure in ordinary usage.
RAZI:91:9/r3.anchor: وقبل القاضي هذا التأويل ، وقال المراد منه أن الله حكم بتزكيتها وسماها بذلك

RAZI:91:9/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:9/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:91:9/r4.claim: The self-purification reading initially seems nearer because “soul” was stated explicitly, while the alternative refers to something only understood as mentioned.
RAZI:91:9/r4.anchor: والأول أقرب ، لأن ذكر النفس قد تقدم ظاهرا ، فرد الضمير عليه أولى

RAZI:91:9/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:9/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:91:9/r5.claim: Because 91:8 was shown to mean that God grants piety and abandons the wicked, this verse must likewise mean that God purifies the soul.
RAZI:91:9/r5.anchor: أن المراد ، بألهمها ما ذكرناه فوجب حمل اللفظ عليه

RAZI:91:9/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:9/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:91:9/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī’s interpretation as mere divine judgment or naming is weak: the verb form denotes bringing about, and a divine judgment cannot change without making truth false and knowledge ignorance.
RAZI:91:9/r6.anchor: لأن بناء التفعيلات على التكوين ، ثم إن سلمنا ذلك لكن ما حكم الله به

RAZI:91:9/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:9/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:91:9/r7.claim: The pronoun should return to the nearer antecedent: the mention of “inspiring it” is nearer than “a soul,” supporting the interpretation just given.
RAZI:91:9/r7.anchor: فإن أهل اللغة اتفقوا على أن عود الضمير إلى الأقرب أولى من عوده إلى الأبعد

RAZI:91:9/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:9/r8.speaker: سعيد بن أبي هلال
RAZI:91:9/r8.claim: Saʿīd b. Abī Hilāl reports that the Prophet paused when reciting this verse and prayed for his soul’s piety and purification, saying God is its guardian and the best to purify it.
RAZI:91:9/r8.anchor: ما رواه الواحدي في البسيط عن سعيد بن أبي هلال أنه عليه السلام كان إذا قرأ

TAB:91:9/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:9/r1.speaker: author
TAB:91:9/r1.claim: The successful person is one whose soul God purifies from disbelief and sins and reforms through righteous deeds.
TAB:91:9/r1.anchor: يقول :  قد أفلح من زكّى اللّهُ نفسَه ،   فكّثر تطهيرها من الكفر والمعاصي ،   وأصلحها بالصالحات من الأعمال .

TAB:91:9/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:9/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:91:9/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the purification as God purifying the person's soul.
TAB:91:9/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكّاها يقول :  قد أفلح من زكّى اللّهُ نفسَه .

TAB:91:9/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:9/r3.speaker: مجاهد، سعيد بن جبير، عكرمة
TAB:91:9/r3.claim: Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and ʿIkrima gloss the phrase as whoever reforms the soul.
TAB:91:9/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد وسعيد بن جُبير وعكرِمة :  قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكّاها قالوا :  من أصلحها .

TAB:91:9/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:9/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:91:9/r4.claim: Qatāda says doing good purifies the soul through obedience to God, or by righteous action.
TAB:91:9/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكّاها من عمل خيرا زكّاها بطاعة الله .

TAB:91:9/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:9/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:91:9/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd also explains the successful person as one whose soul God has purified.
TAB:91:9/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكّاها يقول :  قد أفلح من زكى اللّهُ نفسَه .

TAB:91:9/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:9/r6.speaker: author
TAB:91:9/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī locates the oath's conclusion here, citing Qatāda's explicit statement that the oath falls at “qad aflaḥa man zakkāhā.”
TAB:91:9/r6.anchor: وهذا هو موضع القسم ،   كما :  حدثنا بشر ،   قال :  حدثنا يزيد

ITQAN:v2p487/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p487/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p487/r1.claim: قد enters affirmative, finite, ungoverned verbs; with a past verb it emphasizes realization and can bring a distant past closer to the present.
ITQAN:v2p487/r1.anchor: التحقيق مع الماضي نحو ﴿ قد أفلح المؤمنون ﴾ ﴿ قد أفلح من زكاها ﴾

ITQAN:v3p170/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p170/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p170/r7.claim: The lām of لقد may be dropped where the wording is long.
ITQAN:v3p170/r7.anchor: حذف لام ( لقد ) يحسن مع طول الكلام نحو ﴿ قد أفلح من زكاها ﴾

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r2.claim: To purify the soul is to make it grow and rise through obedience, righteousness, charity, and good works.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r2.anchor: قد أفلح من زكاها يريد أفلح من زكى نفسه، أي: أنماها وأعلاها بالطاعة والبر والصدقة واصطناع المعروف

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r3.claim: The root sense of purification is increase: crops yield abundantly and expenditure is blessed; zakat grows a person's wealth.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r3.anchor: وأصل التزكية: الزيادة، ومنه يقال: زكا الزرع يزكوا: إذا كثر ريعه، وزكت النفقة: إذا بورك فيها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r4.claim: A judge's endorsement of a witness is also called tazkiya because it raises the witness through accreditation and good repute.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r4.anchor: وتزكية القاضي للشاهد منه، لأنه يرفعه بالتعديل والذكر الجميل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r7.claim: Arab benefactors camped conspicuously on hills and lit night fires for visitors, while misers hid in recesses; their habits exemplify raising or burying the self.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r7.anchor: وكانت أجواد العرب تنزل الربا وأيفاع الأرض، لتشتهر أماكنها للمعتفين، وتوقد النيران في الليل للطارقين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r8.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r8.claim: An unnamed poet praises a conspicuous, spacious home that feeds visitors, illustrating the virtue of making oneself known to those seeking hospitality.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر : وبوأت بيتك في معلم ... رحيب المباءة والمسرح كفيت العفاة طلاب القرى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p799/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p799/r3.speaker: قسم من المفسرين
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p799/r3.claim: Some commentators identify qad aflaḥa man zakkāhā as the answer to the oath in Sūrat al-Shams.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p799/r3.anchor: وقسم من المفسرين قال في سورة الشمس أن جواب القسم هو (قد أفلح من زكاها)

NASHR:v1p236/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p236/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p236/r9.claim: Long passages such as the oath sequence in al-Shams can allow stopping at their verse endings through “قد أفلح من زكاها.”
NASHR:v1p236/r9.anchor: ونحو ذلك الوقف على فواصل والشمس وضحاها إلى قد أفلح من زكاها

ALUSI:91:11/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:91:11/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes ‘successful is whoever purified it’ parenthetical after the inspiration clause, not the oath’s answer; he infers an omitted answer that God will destroy Meccan unbelievers for rejecting the Messenger as He destroyed Thamūd for rejecting Ṣāliḥ.
ALUSI:91:11/r2.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري قوله تعالى : { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ } الخ تابعاً لقوله تعالى : { فَأَلْهَمَهَا } الخ

ALUSI:91:11/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the objection that this requires omitting the oath’s lām and improperly emphasizing practical purification over the higher goal of certain belief.
ALUSI:91:11/r3.anchor: فقيل إن ذلك لما يلزم من حذف اللام وأنه لا يليق بالنظم المعجز أن يجعل أدنى الكمالين

ALUSI:91:11/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r4.claim: He replies that deleting the lām is common, especially after a long phrase, and is easier than deleting an entire sentence; al-Zamakhsharī himself accepts an omitted oath answer at 23:1.
ALUSI:91:11/r4.anchor: وقد ذكره في { قد أفلح المؤمنون } [ المرمنون : 1 ] فما حدا مما بدأ وأن التزكية

ALUSI:91:11/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r5.claim: Purification, understood as growth, is not confined to practical action and is itself an intended end, though even a prerequisite may appropriately receive emphasis.
ALUSI:91:11/r5.anchor: وأن التزكية مراداً بها الإنماء لا اختصاص لها وليست مقدمة بل مقصودة بالذات

ALUSI:91:11/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r10.claim: Divine decree does not erase all human agency: even if God ultimately creates the acts, the servant’s participation in purification or corruption suffices for the attribution to him; the text does not prove independent power to choose and create either course.
ALUSI:91:11/r10.anchor: ولا يقتضي ذلك أن لا يكون لقدرة العبد واختياره مدخل في الفجور والتقوى بالكلية

ALUSI:91:11/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:91:11/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the successful soul as one God purifies and guides, and the failed soul as one God corrupts and leads astray; this reading makes God the subject of the purification and corruption verbs.
ALUSI:91:11/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال في ذلك يقول الله تعالى

ALUSI:91:11/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:91:11/r12.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās attributes to the Prophet the explanation that the soul God purifies succeeds and the soul deprived of good fails; it is cited through Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Daylamī without a stated grading.
ALUSI:91:11/r12.anchor: أخرج عنه ابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه والديلمي أنه قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

ALUSI:91:11/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:91:11/r13.claim: Zayd ibn Arqam reports the Prophet’s prayer: asking God to grant the soul piety and purify it, since He is its best purifier, guardian, and master; cited by Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shayba, Muslim, and al-Nasāʾī.
ALUSI:91:11/r13.anchor: عن زيد بن أرقم قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

ALUSI:91:11/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r14.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:91:11/r14.claim: In a report from Ibn ʿAbbās through al-Ṭabarānī and others, the Prophet paused after reciting 91:9 and said the same prayer for the soul’s piety and purification.
ALUSI:91:11/r14.anchor: وفي رواية الطبراني وغيره عن ابن عباس أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام إذا تلا هذه الآية وقف وقال ذلك

ALUSI:91:11/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r15.speaker: صاحب الانتصاف
ALUSI:91:11/r15.claim: The author of al-Intiṣāf prefers taking God as the subject of purification because the pronouns in the preceding oaths then consistently refer to God and because 87:14, with ‘purified’ as a passive-like result, fits that reading.
ALUSI:91:11/r15.anchor: ورجحه صاحب الانتصاف بأن الضمائر في { والسماء وما بناها } [ الشمس : 5 ]

ALUSI:91:11/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r16.claim: Despite those reports, al-Ālūsī says the human-agent reading remains the more immediate sense; the reports do not conclusively establish the alternate subject, but refute al-Zamakhsharī’s charge that it is Sunni ‘inversion’ of the Qadari position.
ALUSI:91:11/r16.anchor: لا ينبغي أن ينكر أن المعنى السابق هو السابق إلى الذهن وما ذكر من الأخبار ليس نصاً في تعيين المعنى الآخر
